{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "BUILD A STATIC NUXT PORTFOLIO WEBSITE – WARM COMMUNITY REAL ESTATE BRAND

Create a premium but friendly static portfolio / marketing website for a local real estate community advisor named "Mara Fieldstone". The site should feel like a warm neighborhood guide + professional property portfolio, not a cold corporate brokerage page. Use Nuxt / Vue components, fully static render, no backend, no login, no database, no real MLS feed, no third-party API. All listings, testimonials, numbers, events, and map-like content can be mock/static sample content.

REFERENCE FEEL
Use Stripe.com as inspiration for structure quality and polish: clean sections, strong cards, smooth gradients, excellent spacing, refined typography, subtle motion, crisp CTA blocks, modular layout, beautiful hover states. But adapt the mood to warm community real estate: soft cream, clay, sage, terracotta, deep espresso text, elegant rounded cards, neighborhood photography placeholders, trust-building copy.

BRAND
Name: Mara Fieldstone Realty
Tagline: Homes, neighborhoods, and belonging.
Tone: warm, expert, grounded, community-first, polished
Audience: families, first-time buyers, downsizers, local sellers, people relocating into a charming town
Location style: fictional area called "Willowmere & Northbank"
Primary color: warm terracotta #C86F4A
Secondary: sage #8FA98B
Background: ivory #FBF6EE
Text: espresso #2E241F
Accent: honey #E7B86A
Soft border: #E9DCCB

MUST BE STATIC ONLY
No real estate API, no live data, no backend, no booking system integration, no account, no forms that actually submit. If there is a contact form, make it static visual only with a note or disabled demo state. Use local arrays / JSON objects / mock content inside the project. No Google Maps embed, instead create a beautiful static illustrated neighborhood map/card section using HTML/CSS only.

OVERALL UX
- Desktop-first but fully responsive mobile layout
- Sticky translucent navigation with warm blur effect
- Smooth anchor scrolling
- Lots of hover effects: cards lift, listing photos zoom, CTA glow, neighborhood tiles reveal extra text, stat cards animate on hover, buttons have Stripe-like gradient shimmer
- Complex layout with many sections, not just a simple landing page
- Use reusable Nuxt components where sensible
- Keep design high-end and realistic

PAGE STRUCTURE

1. TOP NAV
Logo left: small house-line icon + "Mara Fieldstone"
Navigation links:
- Home
- Featured Homes
- Neighborhoods
- Sellers
- Stories
- Process
- Contact
Right CTA button: "Plan a Move"
Hover: nav links underline with terracotta line, CTA gently raises and changes gradient
Mobile: hamburger menu or clean stacked menu is OK, still static

2. HERO SECTION
Layout inspired by Stripe hero: strong left content + rich right visual system
Left:
Small eyebrow badge: Willowmere Community Realtor • Since 2014
Headline: Find the home that feels like part of your story.
Subheadline: A warm, data-informed real estate portfolio for buyers and sellers who care about neighborhood fit, thoughtful guidance, and lasting community.
CTA buttons:
- Explore Featured Homes
- Meet Mara
Trust row:
- 180+ families guided
- 4.9/5 client sentiment
- 12 neighborhood micro-guides
- $72M local volume
Right side:
Create a layered dashboard/card composition, not a single boring photo:
- Main featured home card with placeholder image block / gradient photo style
- Floating market note: "Northbank cottages +8% interest this spring"
- Floating client card: "The Rivera family found a porch within walking distance of school"
- Mini chart card showing warm simple bars for "Buyer match score"
- Small circular avatars made with initials only, no external images needed
Background: soft radial gradients, subtle grid, cream paper texture feel

3. COMMUNITY TRUST STRIP
Horizontal strip under hero with local-style badges:
- Neighborhood walks every Friday
- Seller prep checklist included
- School-distance planning
- Historic homes expertise
- Relocation welcome tours
Make them pill cards with icons and hover color changes.

4. FEATURED HOMES PORTFOLIO
Section title: Featured Homes With A Sense Of Place
Description: Static sample listings curated to show the portfolio style.
Create 6 property cards, mock data only:
A. Maple Porch Cottage – $684,000 – 3 bed / 2 bath – Willowmere
B. The Northbank Brick House – $812,000 – 4 bed / 3 bath – Northbank
C. Sage Lane Bungalow – $529,000 – 2 bed / 2 bath – Garden District
D. Honeywell Courtyard Home – $735,000 – 3 bed / 2.5 bath – Old Mill
E. Elm & Lantern Duplex – $660,000 – 4 bed / 2 bath – East Row
F. The Juniper House – $905,000 – 5 bed / 3.5 bath – Ridgeview
Each card needs:
- Large warm placeholder image panel using CSS gradients or local placeholder div
- Label: Featured / New / Quiet Street / Walkable / Historic / Family Favorite
- Price
- Title
- Details
- Short story-style description
- Small tags: Porch, Garden, School walk, Renovated kitchen etc.
Hover effect: image zoom, card shadow expands, top label slides, CTA appears "View static profile"
Click not required; can be anchor/button only.

5. PROPERTY DETAIL PREVIEW SECTION
A wider editorial feature for one selected home.
Title: Inside The Maple Porch Cottage
Two-column layout:
Left: big image collage grid with three placeholder panels
Right: details card with:
- Why it stands out
- Best for
- Nearby favorites
- Buyer note
- Mock match score 94%
Include a Stripe-style mini metrics panel with rounded cards.

6. NEIGHBORHOOD GUIDE SECTION
Title: Choose The Feeling Of Your Next Chapter
Create 4 neighborhood cards:
- Willowmere: leafy porches, school walks, Sunday market
- Northbank: brick townhomes, coffee corners, river trail
- Old Mill: historic texture, studios, adaptive lofts
- Ridgeview: larger lots, sunset streets, quiet cul-de-sacs
Each card has:
- Mood label
- Average mock price range
- Best for
- Weekend ritual
- Static "walkability" bar
Hover: reveal hidden paragraph and change background gradient
Also include a static illustrated area map: abstract blocks, roads, river line, labels. Use CSS only, no map service.

7. SELLER PORTFOLIO / PRESENTATION SECTION
Title: A Listing Launch That Feels Intentional
Create an elegant process display like a product feature page:
Steps:
1. Home story audit
2. Room-by-room preparation plan
3. Warm editorial photography direction (placeholder only)
4. Pricing narrative & buyer persona mapping
5. Launch week marketing calendar
6. Offer conversation support
Include a mock static launch timeline with day cards:
Day 1 Styling Notes
Day 3 Preview Copy
Day 5 Private Neighbor Share
Day 7 Public Launch
Make hover effects on each step.

8. CASE STUDIES / CLIENT STORIES
Title: Community Stories
Create 3 detailed testimonial case cards:
- "From apartment to garden cottage" – first-time buyers
- "Selling the family home with care" – downsizing sellers
- "Relocating before the school year" – moving family
Each card should include:
- Before situation
- What Mara helped with
- Outcome
- Quote
- Static metric chips (days prepared, offers received, commute improved etc.)
No real client photos needed; use initials avatar circles.

9. STRIPE-LIKE FEATURE GRID
Title: Guidance That Connects The Details
Make a polished 2x3 grid of feature cards with subtle gradients and mini UI mockups:
- Buyer Match Notes: compare lifestyle priorities
- Seller Prep Board: static checklist UI
- Neighborhood Rhythm: weekly routine planner
- Offer Clarity: simple offer comparison mock visual
- Move Timeline: milestone cards
- After-Close Welcome: local resource packet
This is only visual/static. Make the cards feel premium and interactive with hover lift, border glow, and background movement.

10. MARKET SNAPSHOT STATIC SECTION
Title: A Calm View Of The Local Market
Use only sample data. Add a clear tiny note: "Illustrative sample data for design preview."
Create chart-like visuals using CSS/HTML:
- Median price trend bars
- Buyer demand meter
- Inventory cards
- Average prep timeline
- Neighborhood comparison table
No chart library required unless simple; CSS bars are fine.

11. ABOUT MARA SECTION
Warm editorial bio:
Headline: Local Knowledge, Human Pace
Text: Mara combines neighborhood-level research with the patient listening of someone who actually lives where she works. Her portfolio focuses on homes that match routines, not just search filters.
Include:
- Portrait placeholder card
- Credentials list
- Community involvement list: school garden sponsor, porch concert volunteer, first-time buyer workshops
- Quote pullout
Hover: credentials cards lift.

12. RESOURCE LIBRARY STATIC CARDS
Title: Helpful Guides Before You Move
Create 6 static article/resource cards:
- The Porch Test: How To Judge A Street In 10 Minutes
- First-Time Buyer Warm Start Checklist
- What To Fix Before Listing A Character Home
- Northbank Coffee Walk Map (Static Guide)
- Downsizing Without Rushing The Goodbye
- How To Compare Homes Beyond Square Footage
Each card has category, read time, description, hover underline CTA "Read guide". Links can be placeholder anchors.

13. CONTACT / CTA SECTION
Big warm CTA panel:
Headline: Let’s talk about the kind of life your next home should support.
Subtext: Share a little about your timeline, your neighborhood hopes, and what home means to you.
Buttons:
- Start A Conversation
- Download Seller Prep List
Static visual contact form with fields:
- Name
- Email
- Moving timeline
- I’m interested in: Buying / Selling / Both / Just exploring
- Message
But no submit backend. Button can say "Demo form only" or show a small note: "Static preview, no message is sent."

14. FOOTER
Columns:
Brand + mini description
Explore: Featured Homes, Neighborhoods, Seller Process, Stories
Resources: Buyer Guide, Seller Checklist, Community Notes
Contact: hello@marafieldstone.example, Willowmere Studio, by appointment
Add disclaimer: Static portfolio concept. Listings and market information are sample content.

DESIGN DETAILS
Typography:
Use elegant sans + optional serif for headings if available. If using Google fonts would require external dependency, okay to use CSS font stack instead. Good combinations:
- Headings: Georgia / Playfair-like fallback
- Body: Inter-like system sans

Visual style:
- Warm gradients
- Rounded 24px/32px cards
- Soft shadows, not harsh
- Thin borders
- Subtle background grid or topographic lines using CSS
- Premium spacing similar to Stripe landing pages
- Section transitions with overlapping cards
- Lots of micro-interactions on hover only, no complex JS required

COMPONENT IDEAS
Please organize with components if possible:
- AppHeader
- HeroCommunity
- TrustStrip
- FeaturedListings
- ListingCard
- NeighborhoodGuide
- SellerProcess
- StoryCards
- FeatureGrid
- MarketSnapshot
- AboutMara
- ResourceLibrary
- ContactCTA
- AppFooter

CONTENT QUALITY
Please write realistic copy, not lorem ipsum. Make the real estate content feel local, thoughtful, and believable. The site is for a portfolio and brand presentation, so the copy should sell expertise and community care.

INTERACTIONS
Required hover effects:
- Nav links animated underline
- CTA buttons gradient shift / lift
- Listing cards lift + image scale
- Neighborhood cards reveal extra description
- Process cards highlight connected timeline
- Feature grid cards border glow
- Resource cards CTA slide
- Footer links color transition
Optional: gentle entrance animations are fine if CSS only.

RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS
- Mobile hero stacks cleanly
- Listing grid becomes 1 column on small screens, 2 on tablet, 3 desktop
- Neighborhood map stays readable or becomes scrollable/card-like
- Header remains usable on mobile
- CTA form stacks fields

DELIVERABLE
Create the static Nuxt site with polished styling. It should run as a static front-end demo with mock content only. Do not add backend services, real API keys, authentication, database, or live external integrations. Keep it self-contained and visually complete.",

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
